newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Electrometals in WMC copper pact.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Electrometals in WMC copper pact.

text.p: Electrometals Mining Ltd said on Tuesday it entered into an agreement for WMC Ltd to fund fast-track development of enhanced copper electrowinning technology in exchange for a right to use the technology.

After completing a two-year development programme, WMC will have the right to use the technology on copper projects containing reserves in excess of 100,000 tonnes of copper metal and on waste streams generated by their own operations in exchange for a license fee, Tony Treasure, managing director of Electrometals, told Reuters.
WMC has copper mining operations at Olympic Dam in South Australia and Nifty in Western Australia.

Treasure said the process has the potential for wider use among the 20 percent to 25 percent of the world's copper industry which mines copper through the solvent extraction-electrowinning, or non-smelted process.
Deeper copper deposits typically require smelting to produce metal, while shallower reserves and recycled mine tailings are more adaptable to electro-winning.
"We haven't replaced electro-winning, we've just turbo-charged it," Treasure said.
The goal of the work funded by WMC is to establish the technology as a viable alternative to conventional electrowinning on medium to large-sized deposits, he said.
Electrometals is free to develop or license the enhanced technology on coppper projects producing under 100,000 tonnes, Treasure said.
The technology already has been successfully applied to small to medium-sized copper projects, he said.
Subject to the success of the programme on copper, the technology could be extended to other metals, he added.
